*“The potential applications are astounding. Diagnostic analysis in multiple fields. Extradimensional maps of staggering precision. Weapons.”*

*“So that’s it,” you say. “That’s why the agency’s so interested in Innsmouth.”*

*“Well, the Order’s supernatural and criminal activities* did *warrant a federal investigation. I came in later. But yes,” says Elina. “Now you know everything. That’s it.”*

interlude4.guardianDispatched:
*Despite the flooding coast, the waters are calm. As you watch the waves, the dream of the Deep One comes back to you, unbidden. Nested within that dream is another—the dream of gliding through voids, of crisscrossing between untold fathoms and fathomless dimensions. You’ve glimpsed it before. But now the dream is tinged with the dreamer’s alien grief.*

*“It’s dead,” you say.*

*“What is?” Elina asks.*

*“The city’s guardian. These creatures and their gods are not invulnerable. Their city is undefended.”*
interlude4.wavewornIdol:
*“This is one of the crystals, I take it,” you say, showing Elina the idol with the sea- green stone.*

*“Indeed,” she says. “A phenomenal example. Let’s not lose it.”*

*“You think we’ll survive this?” you ask.*

*“Not really. But just in case.”*

*You caress the alien alloy and once again manipulate the idol’s strange prongs. A faint force tugs at the statue, as if a child were trying to pull it from your hands. It tugs in the direction of Devil Reef.*
interlude4.awakenedMantle:
*Elina rubs the fabric between her forefinger and thumb. “Unpleasant. You are right. It feels like skin.”*

*She lets it go. There is no wind, not even much of a breeze, but the mantle suddenly billows out like a sail. You catch it just before it blows away. The boat picks up speed.*

*“Astonishing,” says Elina. “It wants to take us back to where it came from.”*
interlude4.headdressOfYhaNthlei:
*Elina examines the headdress, brushing the crystals adorning it with her fingertips.*

*“It’s just like the tiara. An exact replica.”*

*“Not made for a human head,” you say after she hands it back to you. You think back to the strange priestess. The memory troubles you. A faint force tugs at the crown, as if a child were trying to pull it from your hands. It tugs in the direction of Devil Reef.*

intro.ignore: _ACT_ Ignore the Italicized text on _Act 2a: City of the Deep (v. II)_ and its reverse side, _Act 2b: Conspiracy Fulfilled_.
intro.body:
*You don’t know if memory, dream, or otherworldly propulsion steers your boat to the islet that is Y’ha- nthlei’s vestibule. When the craft floats to a standstill in a sheltered deepwater nook, you tie it to an outcropping and disembark. At hand is a well- worn path that you’re sure you’ve never seen before. You and Elina accept the ominous conveniences in silence. You are not surprised when the path takes you to a cave.*

*“If my maps are accurate,” Elina says, “I believe we are going somewhere where the normal laws don’t apply. Things are already strange—a sun and moon that don’t move, a ship that steers itself…I don’t know what we can do to stop all this, but I will say this: These beings may thrive in the water and build their palaces in it, but it is not theirs. Water is the earth’s. It is not an extradimensional substance. It gives homes to creatures with biological needs more or less similar to our own. It stores heat and helps regulate the atmosphere. It contributes to the balance that has allowed so many species in our world to flourish. It does not want to be in a place of gods and demons; it wants to be with us.”*
intro.awakenedMantle:
*“Think of how that mantle your found repels water. Not as a raincoat or umbrella does, but as if the water had no business with it.”*

*“Insightful. But how can it help?” you ask.*

*“I don’t know, exactly. But if, as I believe, physical laws work differently below, then the water may be more willing to flow away from the city than it is to flow into it. Surely, some eldritch mechanism keeps it there; perhaps some clue will show us how to reverse it.”*

flashback14.body:
Flashback XIV

*Dawson led you from the Lair of Dagon to another huge chamber. Twin waterfalls emptied into a pool in its center. A massive shape slept within it.*

*“I thought so…” murmured Dawson. “Two gods.”*

*“Was this the other task? Seeing this?”*

*“Yes. Recon. We had to be sure what we read was true. Elina would be amazed. This place is beyond anything—It makes me strangely sad.”*

*“Why?”*

*“It’ll have to be destroyed, of course.”*

*“Who’s going to do that?”*

*“We will—Not us personally. The military. It’s too dangerous. Innsmouth, too—but that will be more surgical.”*

*“Oh,” you said, after a moment. “That makes sense.” It was more than reasonable, given what you’d seen. Necessary. Still, it came as a shock. Once again, you had been kept in the dark.*

*“How is it going to happen?” you asked.*

*“We have a dozen submarines to the east armed with torpedoes. And we have a squadron of eight battleships nearby, too.” Despite his reservations, Dawson couldn’t keep the pride out of his voice.*

*“N*O*. I* FORBID IT*,” you said firmly. “I* WAS DREAMING IN THE GARDEN*,* WAITING FOR MY SIRE*,* MY SON*,* MY SPOUSE*.”*

*“Come again?” said Dawson.*

*“I* SHOWED YOU HOSPITALITY*! I* LET YOU TAKE FIGS FROM THE TREES*;* MY HANDMAIDS RUBBED YOU DOWN WITH OILS*; I* WOULD HAVE SENT YOU AWAY WITH GREAT GIFTS*.”*

*Dawson’s hand went to his gun, but you knew he would never shoot you.*

*“D*AGON WOULD HAVE DRIVEN YOU AWAY*. B*UT THE SLEEP WE ENJOYED WAS LOVELY*,* THE SHADY LAPPING WATER SO LULLING AND SWEET*…I* HAVE

*ALWAYS BEEN MORE POWERFUL IN PATIENCE THAN*

HE*. O*UR TIME IS COMING*;* WHY HURRY IT*? B*UT NOW MY HOSPITALITY IS REPAID WITH BETRAYAL*. Y*OU WOULD TAKE MY GIFTS AND TURN ON ME*!”*

*Then you lunged at Dawson and knocked him into the pool. He leapt out and wrestled you to the ground.*

*“Stop! Snap out of it,” he said.*

*You tumbled across the chamber floor, grasping, wheezing, flailing. At the same time, you fought the voice that had made you its mouth and called to you in so many dreams.*

*Your will was divided. Your body thrashed between commands. But eventually, right when Dawson got the best of you, you came back into yourself. You relaxed. Dawson’s stranglehold relaxed too.*

*“Is it really you?” he breathed.*

*“Who are you?” you asked.*

*That was when Oceiros Marsh found you.*

ψ

*You clutch your head.*

*“What is it?” asks Elina.*

*“Dawson—here—I attacked him. I was— possessed. That’s how I lost my memory. I didn’t hurt him—But—How awful. That voice—”*

*Elina watches you apprehensively. “You are all right now?*

*“Yes.”*

*“And your memory?”*

*“Still incomplete, but I remember more… Dawson told me about the battleships. You said you’d told me everything, but you didn’t.”*

*“That’s not* our *job. The Navy will do it.”*

*“It would have been nice to know.”*

*“There are lots of things it would be nice to know. Other things—very nice not to know. But listen. We don’t have much time. We need to take what we can.”*

*“The crystals?”*

*“Yes.”*

*“Do you really think we should bring anything from this place back with us?”*

*“The weapons pointed at Y’ha-nthlei are ones I helped develop using these materials. Pandora has opened the box. Was it wrong of me? I was stumbling in the darkness and found something that looked very much like light. I saw what it illuminated and shared it with people I trust. The more I looked, the more disturbing I saw it to be— but I can’t pretend I didn’t see it. I can’t—we can’t—put ourselves in some paradise of ignorance. I understand the impulse—I do! But we can’t choose that. If we forget, someone else will remember—and they will have power over us. You who forgot everything know what that’s like.”*

*“Yes I do. Too well,” you say.*

In your Campaign Log, under “Memories Recovered,” record *a stinging betrayal.*

The investigators must decide (choose one):

  • Help Agent Harper complete her mission. Put the set-aside City of the Deep (v. II) into play next to the current act. It provides a new alternate objective.
  • Defy Agent Harper. Search each player’s hand, deck, discard pile, and all play areas for Elina Harper and remove her from the game. Put the set-aside City of the Deep (v. III) into play next to the current act. It provides a new alternate objective.

noResolution.body: _If no resolution was reached because each investigator was defeated_: *You are dying. You cannot tell if you are underwater or breathing, bleeding, or suffocating. You hear the voice you used to hear in dreams, but it does not call to you. It sings its song as you die, and nothing in its song changes when you do. The song goes on, and Y’ha- nthlei swallows your body. You are and have always been a skeleton on the sunless floor of the ocean.*

resolution1.body: _Resolution 1_: *You swim upward, through the maelstrom, to the mundane realm you left behind. When your head emerges from the cold and exhilarating Atlantic, you bellow. Seabirds cry out in response. The islet where you began your descent is only a few yards away. Your boat is still there.*

resolution2.body: _Resolution 2_: *It is midmorning—who knows what day. The sky is blue, and the sun is no longer chained to the moon. The waters are placid.*

resolution3.body: _Resolution 3_: *The sun shines overhead, but it shines in a crimson sky, chained to the moon. The waters surge around you.*

resolution4.body:
_Resolution 4_: *You make your way to the boat. Elina gets there before you, buoyed by her success.*

*“We found so much crystal,” she says. “And, more importantly, we prevented a great catastrophe.”*

*“I only hope this wasn’t just a prelude to a different catastrophe,” you say, holding out one of the crystals meaningfully.*

*“In this universe, everything is a prelude to a catastrophe,” she says. “But—I understand your concern. Believe me, I share it. I will be careful and do my best to ensure that the others engaged in this work are too.”*

resolution5.body:
_Resolution 5_: *You make your way to the boat, where Elina is waiting for you.*

*“A fool’s errand,” she says. “You destroyed the vaults?”*

*“Yes, and everything they held.”*

*“Nothing a torpedo couldn’t have done or won’t do, I imagine, but I’m glad you had the personal satisfaction of risking your life for a noble cause.”*

*“Don’t be bitter, Elina. It was the right decision.”*

*“I understand your perspective,” she says, sounding rather tired. “Anyway, there’s no use debating it now.”*

resolution6.body:
_Resolution 6_: *You make your way to the boat. Elina gets there before you, buoyed by her success.*

*“We found so many,” she says, admiring a few of the sea-green crystals in her hand.*

*“We did. But I think we might have lost the world along the way.”*

*“I know.” She puts them down and fires a flare into the sky. “I hope someone from the Navy sees that.”*

*“What will we do now?”*

*“We’ll board a battleship, if we’re lucky.”*

*“And then?”*

*“What else? Battle.”*

resolution7.body:
_Resolution 7_: *You make your way to the boat, where Elina is waiting for you.*

*“A fool’s errand,” she says. “You destroyed the vaults?”*

*“Yes, and everything they held.”*

*“Nothing a torpedo couldn’t have done or won’t do, I imagine, but I’m glad you had the personal satisfaction of risking your life for a noble cause. Meanwhile, the sun and the moon continue their obsession with each other.”*

*“I saw,” you say.*

*Elina fires a flare into the sky. “I hope someone from the Navy sees that.”*

*“What will we do now?”*

*“We’ll board a battleship.”*

*“And then?”*

*“Find all the animals we can, pack them onto the boat, and wait for a rainbow.”*

*“We’ll be waiting a long time,” you say.*

*“A long time? Only if we’re lucky.”*

resolution8.body:
_Resolution 8_: *You are among the first victims of the deluge. The waters rise inch by inch at first, then foot by foot, then tower by tower, on the last day covering the tip of Sagarmatha, and then drowning even the memory of land. Hordes attack the vessels with which some people seek to save themselves. A thousand desperate armadas sink to the ocean floor. The skies are filled with frantic birds for several weeks. Then they empty of life, and starlight and moonlight and sunlight pour down on a world where nothing breathes.*

*And still the waters rise. The springs are infinite. Hydra and Dagon dip their ladles in the ever- flowing fountain of brine and ooze. They are the cupbearers of all the Old Ones, and they wait for the exiles to come to repossess the reality that was and is to be theirs, sailing in on their great ships. Unhearable choruses sing the name Cthulhu. The stars shudder.*

*G*LORY TO *D*AGON*! G*LORY TO *H*YDRA*! G*LORY TO *Y’*HA*-*NTHLEI*,* PORT OF THE *O*LD *O*NES*! I*T IS YOUR TIME*.*

epilogue.ifAllFourteen: If all 14 of the entries listed on p. 54 of the campaign guide are listed under “Memories Recovered,” proceed to _Flashback XV_. Otherwise, read no further.

epilogue1.body:
*You are back in Boston’s Custom House tower, in the office where you met Dawson. Now you sit where Dawson sat. The photograph of him and the other soldiers at the Bellicourt Tunnel is still there. It would have been sacrilege to remove it. You never wanted Dawson’s job—the idea had never occurred to you—but your role in the Innsmouth affair impressed the agency, and the secrets you knew made the higher-ups eager to keep their eyes on you. You have been surprised to discover how well-suited you are for it, how you can pour yourself into it. Of course, the memories of that month sometimes distract you. When that happens, the other agents know not to bother you. Now is one of those times. Even so, someone knocks on the door.*

*“It’s open,” you call. “Why, Agent Harper!”*

*“Agent Harper?” she says, striding in. “Don’t be ridiculous.”*

*“Elina,” you say.*

*“I’m so happy to see you. You look well.”*

*“Don’t lie to me. There was enough of that back in Innsmouth.”*

*“I’m sorry. I* am *happy to see you, though. How are you? I got your letter, you know.”*

*“I’m still having flashbacks. I see him all the time— Dawson, I mean. And I still dream the dreams of the Deep Ones. It’s taking its toll.”*

*“I know. Me too, now. I thought it would get better, not worse. I’ve—talked to someone.”*

*“How’d that go?”*

*“It was absurd. A Freudian. I couldn’t do it. Everything was about fathers and mothers and nothing that actually happened.”*

*“This is about fathers and mothers, in a way,” you say.*

*“What? Oh. Yes. Father Dagon. Mother Hydra. Listen. I came to town to show you something. Clear some space on your desk.”*

*You do, and she unrolls and spreads out a large map.*

*“The sea floor? Where? What are those big white spots?” you ask, pointing to a line in the middle of the map.*

*“That’s Devil Reef. This is a composite of images I made last August and September.”*

*“Now I understand why I couldn’t read it. It’s Y’ha- nthlei.”*

*“Yes. An elevation map, but the surfaces measured occupy subaquatic, subterranean, and— extradimensional layers. Now—call in your secretary.”*

*“What?”*

*“Humor me.”*

*You did as Elina asked and introduced the two. Elina pointed to the map. “I’m curious, Miss McComb—What do you see?”*

*Miss McComb looked at the map. “What? On that sheet?”*

*“Yes.”*

*“Why, nothing,” she said. “It’s just a blank piece of paper.”*

flashback15.body:
Flashback XV

ψ ψ

*“This is the Temple of the Union,” intoned a priestess in silver and green dress. Silver fins ran up and down her arms, and her eyes continually bled silver. Loops of pearl and sea-green crystals hung over her breasts, and on her head was a platinum crown or coronet. She had two fishtails, one predominantly white, one predominantly black, both mottled with the opposite color. “Reconcile with us. You have heard Mother’s call.”*

*You knew you had mere moments. You were drowning—not in water, but in the inhospitable ether of a reality hostile to yours.*

*So, when she reached out to you, you had not slapped her hand and made her recoil; you had not stolen her headdress and fled the temple. Instead, you had let her take your hand. You had let her lead you away from the semicircle of phantoms to a place of profound mysteries and silver paths. You had let her instruct you in remembering and forgetting.*

*Because you had known—when she reached out to you—that hers was the hand of someone who wanted to save you.*

ψ ψ

*There was a city in the ocean. Its towers shunned the sky. Its streets were meaningless labyrinths. Its people were not people at all. But its courtyards, palaces, porches, and halls glowed with azure, aquamarine, and turquoise. Its walls and floors and ceilings were mosaics of light and shadow. Bridges crossed abysses; wells and fissures went down to the stars; and in its temples you might kneel to indifferent but utterly real gods. Then came the torpedoes and the slag and the sludge, the hot ocean, and the trash; the people and their noises; the planes overhead; ship after ship of endless cargo. More heat. More noise. Then silence.*

*Then, finally, the city rose again.*

*G*LORY TO *D*AGON*! G*LORY TO *H*YDRA*! G*LORY TO *Y’*HA*-*NTHLEI*,* PORT OF THE *O*LD *O*NES*! I*T IS YOUR TIME*.*

In your Campaign Log, under “Memories Recovered,” record *the horrible truth.*

sections.title: Translator’s Note
text: *Encouraged by the reception of my first translation in this vein—and by reception I mean some scattered applause, no actual objections, and just a hint of forbearance—I ventured into the uncharted seas of a project twice that one in scope and audacity; in doing so I was like one who, having learned to tread water, sets out to swim the Bosporus or who, having mastered canoeing, goes to Nantucket to captain a whaler. Yet, here I am, neither drowned nor dashed against the rocks. I have made it to that far shore. I hope you will join me.—Olaus Wormius*

sections.title: Preface
text: Like *The Dunwich Legacy of Olaus Wormius*, *The Innsmouth Conspiracy of Olaus Wormius* is a reworking of the storytelling in an Arkham Horror campaign guide—this time, *The Innsmouth Conspiracy*. It changes nothing mechanically about the campaign and—with some minor, flagged exceptions—is compatible with the parts of the story told on the campaign’s scenario cards.

As with the first reworking, my primary goal was to change the style of *Innsmouth*’s writing. The changes I made are consistent with what I did there, but revising *TIC* came with new challenges. Because there was more writing, there was more to rewrite. The more I did, the more radically *Innsmouth* changed. The plot is, broadly speaking, the same—it has to be to maintain compatibility between the story and the game. But it differs in the details, sometimes quite a bit.

Outside style, the most important changes I made were to the characters and storylines of Elina Harper and Thomas Dawson. These characters have been almost completely reimagined. I wanted to make them seem more like real people and their mission in Innsmouth more plausible.

As with *Dunwich*, I have incorporated footnotes addressing connections or inconsistencies between *TIC* and Lovecraft’s *Shadow Over Innsmouth*. There aren’t as many of these because the plots of *TIC* and Lovecraft’s story are less inextricable than the plots of *The Dunwich Horror* and *TDL*.

Finally, I have to admit: I don’t think fish people are scary. (If I happened to see a fish person, I’d probably feel different.) But the ocean—the ocean is terrifying and endlessly compelling. Another goal of mine was to make it more of a presence—deep, cruel, eternal, fragile.

sections.title: How To Use
text: Instead of reading the narrative blocks at the beginning of scenarios, in scenario resolutions, and in flashbacks, read this instead. I direct you back to *The Innsmouth Conspiracy Campaign Guide* when you have a choice to make, something to note in the campaign log, etc. In other words, nothing affecting the mechanics of the card game happens in *The Innsmouth Conspiracy of Olaus Wormius*, but everything story-related occurring outside the round structure of the card game does. Grayed out blocks of text typically contain optional or conditional readings. Sometimes these blocks come between pieces of non-blocked text. Make sure you continue reading any text that follows such a block.

In *The Dunwich Legacy of Olaus Wormius*, I added a new interlude for the sake of pacing and to give players an opportunity to play a side story. I didn’t do anything like that here: *Innsmouth* has enough interludes, and as far side stories go, *Innsmouth*’s frequent dips into the past make almost any side story reasonable as a memory coming back to the investigator.
Very rarely, at the beginning of a scenario, I direct you to ignore certain flavor text on Act and/or Agenda cards. I only made this intervention when style *and* plot made it necessary.

Finally, *TIC* makes less narrative sense for a group of investigators than it does for one. You wake up together, all of you with amnesia about the same things; you experience collective, simultaneous flashbacks; as you trudge along the coast, you pass out (again simultaneously) several times and have other, more epic collective flashbacks. There are ways you can help your imagination sidestep some of these absurdities—the player instructed to read the flashback controls the investigator who has it; the Lead Investigator is the one who passes out, and then they inform the others of what happened—but the default narrative simply favors a solo investigator. I have left this situation exactly as I found it.
Two small extra notes—1) I didn’t change any of the campaign guide’s Key descriptions. 2) I made flashbacks and scenarios happening before the campaign’s start date use past tense.

sections.title: Disclaimer
text: This is a labor of love and interpretation and reflects my own sensibilities. I in no way want to suggest that the original is not good enough, but to supplement it with a variation, a “take,” that, after all, owes everything to the existence of that original. My hope is that I give players yet another reason to replay *Innsmouth* and that they find the return both familiar and wholly new.

sections.title: Acknowledgments
text: I admire and deeply appreciate the work of the designers and writers of *The Innsmouth Conspiracy.* The settings and mechanics in several of the campaign’s scenarios are some of the most richly imagined pieces of game design I have ever seen. Thanks to Maxine Newman and everyone else who worked on this expansion. And much gratitude to everyone on the current Arkham Horror design team, for continuing to create and to support the best game in this dimension. I would also like to thank Michael Wang for enduring, critiquing, and complimenting what I shared with him, Max McDonald for reading the drafts of this guide and *Dunwich*, and Arturo Hale and Nisha Dhariwal for helping me kind of understand piezoelectricity.

sections.title: Timeline
text: The timeline of the *TIC* has inconsistencies. The campaign gives us three specific dates as well as several incidental remarks that introduce discrepancies. My initial inclination was to use one of the set dates and work from that, but any choice I made would be arbitrary. So instead I chose to jettison the original timeline altogether in favor of one built around a concrete date that made narrative sense—Sunday, September 11, 1927, when there was a full moon.[^5] This and the following day, September 12th, would be the date of the syzygy and the campaign’s final scenarios. This had the effect of compressing the adventure’s calendar, which also makes narrative sense. Also included are the dates Lovecraft uses in *The Shadow over Innsmouth*.
July 1927
Saturday the 16th. The narrator of *SOI* flees Innsmouth.
Sunday the 17th. The narrator of *SOI* speaks to government officials in Arkham.
Monday the 18th. The narrator of *SOI* speaks to government officials in Boston.
Tuesday the 19th. Agent Thomas Dawson, having been gathering intelligence on Innsmouth for the past few months, decides it’s time to take action.
Wednesday the 20th. The government seizes the tiara in the Newburyport Historical Society’s collection.
Monday the 25th. The government begins vetting people who seem psychically sensitive to the rumblings in Innsmouth. Agent Elina Harper joins the investigation.
Wednesday the 27th. Harper lodges at the Gilman House in Innsmouth.
August 1927
Friday the 5th. Harper is kidnapped.
Monday the 15th. Dawson and the Lead Investigator meet in Boston. The Lead Investigator takes the job. Flashback I.
Wednesday the 17th. The events of *The Vanishing of Elina Harper*. Flashback II.
Friday the 19th. If *the mission was a failure*, this is the day that Harper escapes her kidnapper and meets the Lead Investigator.
Sunday the 21st. The kidnapper escapes. The protagonists decide to lodge in nearby Ipswich, feeling they are being watched too closely in Innsmouth. Flashback VIII.
Friday the 26th. The protagonists debate how to proceed in their investigation of Devil Reef and the Esoteric Order of Dagon. Flashback VII.
Wednesday the 31st. Dawson and the Lead Investigator return to Innsmouth, renting rooms at the Gilman House.
September 1927
Thursday the 1st. Dawson and the Lead Investigator break into the Little Bookshop. Flashback VI.
Friday the 2nd. The events of *Devil Reef*. Flashbacks IX-XII and Flashback XV.
Saturday the 3rd. Dawson sends a message to Harper about what happened at Devil Reef and informs her that he and the Lead Investigator intend to break into the Esoteric Order of Dagon.
Sunday the 4th. Flashback V.
Monday the 5th – Tuesday the 6th. The events of *The Lair of Dagon*. Flashbacks IV and XIV. The agency procures a boat and new lodgings for Harper in Innsmouth.
Wednesday the 7th. Harper returns to Innsmouth.
Saturday the 10th. The events of *The Pit of Despair.*
Sunday the 11th. The events of *In Too Deep* and *Horror in High Gear*.
Monday the 12th. The events of *A Light in the Fog* and *Into the Maelstrom*.

notes: [^5] The syzygy should probably involve a new moon, but *TIC*’s is definitely full (pp. 7, 31), and I kept it that way.
